❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) & Local CLI Guide

Q: Is this an official Google Cloud website or product?

  • No. This is an unofficial tool and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Google LLC or Google Cloud.
  • While data is automatically harvested from public Google Cloud feeds and Discovery APIs, it is provided "as-is" without warranty. Always refer to the Official Google Cloud Locations Page, Vertex AI Model Locations Documentation, Compute Engine Regions & Zones Documentation, and Official Google Cloud Documentation for the latest information.

Q: What happens when Google Cloud launches a brand-new service, AI model, region, zone, or API?

  • Zero-Touch Dynamic Discovery: Every daily harvest dynamically pulls the live product/region feeds (data.json, locations_map.json, multi-region-data.json, global-data.json), live Vertex AI model availability tables, live Compute Engine zone/GPU tables, and the live Google APIs Discovery directory (discovery.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis).
  • Any newly launched service, AI model, region, zone, machine series, GPU, or REST API is automatically ingested, matched via documentation URL slug and title similarity, given its own detail view, and highlighted in the What's New tab without requiring any code changes.

Q: How often is the data refreshed, and how are API quota issues prevented?

  • By default, the dataset is refreshed once per day (24-hour TTL = 86,400 seconds).
  • All UI interactions, searches, AI model checks, region comparisons, and CLI queries read from the local cache (data/cache/gcp_catalog.json) and pre-rendered static HTML files in dist/—making zero external API calls during normal usage.
  • When the daily harvest runs, ResilientFetcher enforces a token-bucket rate limit, checkpoints every individual API specification to disk, and automatically retries any 429 / 403 / 5xx responses using exponential backoff with full jitter.

Q: How do I run the application locally?

# 1. Start the local web server (serves dist/ + REST API + daily auto-refresh thread)
python3 server.py --port 8080

# 2. Or open the static HTML files directly in any browser:
open dist/index.html

# 3. Query Services, Regions, or AI Models from the terminal using cli.py:
python3 cli.py service "Vertex AI"
python3 cli.py service alloydb
python3 cli.py models gemini
python3 cli.py models claude --region us-east5
python3 cli.py region us-central1
python3 cli.py region asia-south1
python3 cli.py compare us-central1 europe-west1 asia-south1 --diff

# 4. Force an immediate live re-harvest & static site rebuild:
python3 cli.py refresh --force
